newsitem.title: PERU: Lima share prices end down in apathetic trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima share prices end down in apathetic trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down in low volume on Thursday, maintaining the market's recent trend of insipid trade as investors continued to be concerned over the economy's slow growth, brokers said.
They added the exchange was unlikley to see any improvements in the short term.
Thursday, the General Index .IGRA fell 0.31 percent to 1,442.3 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dropped 0.85 percent to 2,022.2 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
"Today (Thursday) we returned to the familiar path of gently falling prices," said Luis Cueva of the local brokerage Argos, after the market experienced a small technical rebound Wednesday.
The recent slump on the market has been due to the economy's slow growth.
Earlier this week, Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress the government estimated the economy would grow around 2.5 percent this year, down from 7.0 percent last year.
This would be well down on the government's original six- percent growth estimate for the year and also below the bottom- end goal of three percent agreed with the IMF mid-way through 1996.
Thursday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed down 1.14 percent at 5.21 soles, in volume of 661,000 shares, according to preliminary figures.
Tin miner Minsur fared worse because of insecurity over future tin prices, brokers said. The company's price fell 2.65 percent to 21.70 soles on volume of 45,000 shares.

Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start Monday, bucked the day's trend, climbing 1.19 percent to 3.40 soles on small volume of 48,000 shares.
In a total of 1,170 trades, volume was estimated at 15.2 million soles ($5.9 million)
